get.summary:
The caller's team's Automations, newest first, and whether the caller
administers the team. A person on no team has none.

post.summary:
Make an Automation of the caller's team, which starts Runs as the
caller, with their permissions, each time its trigger fires. Only the
caller in their own signed-in session makes one (403 otherwise), and
its Runs must be ones they could start now. A schedule, a repository
event and a Task event are a routine of the caller's, which the
scheduler must take (400 with its reason otherwise); a webhook's secret
is in the answer, once.

Fire the Automation whose routine this run is: only the code step of a
run of an Automation's routine calls it, with the credential the
scheduler signed for the routine (403 for any other caller). It starts
a Run as the Automation's creator, once per routine run, unless the
Automation is switched off, the queue is full or a Run already runs on
the task.

delete.summary:
Delete an Automation of the caller's team, its creator's or, for an
admin of the team, any, and its routine. The Runs it started keep the record of it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Automation's id.

put.summary:
Switch an Automation of the caller's team on or off. Only its creator
switches it on, in their own signed-in session, as for making it; its
creator or an admin of the team switches it off (403 otherwise). Its
routine follows.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Automation's id.

post.summary:
Fire a webhook Automation. The call carries no login: it is signed with
the Automation's secret, as Macro signs its own webhooks
(`x-macro-signature: v1=<hex>`, an HMAC-SHA256 of
`"{x-macro-timestamp}.{body}"`), at a timestamp (Unix seconds) within
five minutes of now (401 otherwise, as for an id no webhook has). The
same timestamp and body received before is refused (409), however its
digest is spelled, so a replay starts nothing. The body is empty, or JSON naming the
task the Run works on.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Automation's id.

get.summary: List the built-in Flows a Run can be started of, by name.

post.summary:
Hand back the result of the factory Step the calling agent session works
on. The session's latest hand back is the Step's result once its turn
ends.

get.summary:
How the caller's own Runs went over a period: Runs by day, outcome and
Flow, how long Runs and Steps took, how often each entry failed or was
visited again, and the tokens their agents used. At most the newest
1,000 Runs of the period are read.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The period's first day, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Its last day, included. The period lasts at most 366 days.

parameters.name: timeZone
parameters.description: The IANA time zone the days are in, such as `Europe/Lisbon`.

parameters.name: flow
parameters.description: A built-in Flow's name, to read only its Runs.

get.summary:
List a page of the factory's board: the Runs the caller can see,
theirs or their team's, newest first, each with its Steps and where it
is (`running`, `waiting` on its owner at a Gate, `held` by a Main Hold,
`stopped` for a person, or `finished`). Read the next page with `next`.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description:
Whose Runs: the caller's (`mine`, when left out), or their team's
(`team`), which lists the members' Runs on tasks the caller can see.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only Runs there.

parameters.name: flow
parameters.description: Only Runs of this built-in Flow, by name.

parameters.name: repoUrl
parameters.description:
Only Runs on this repository, by its `https://github.com/owner/name`
URL.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description:
Only Runs whose task was in this Project (an initiative) when they
started.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description:
Only Runs whose request, or whose task's name, has these words in
it, in any case: at most 200 characters are read.

parameters.name: afterCreatedAt
parameters.description: Where the page starts: the `next.createdAt` of the page before.

parameters.name: afterId
parameters.description:
The `next.id` of the page before: given with `afterCreatedAt` or
not at all (400 otherwise).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most Runs the page lists: 25 when left out, at most 50.

post.summary:
Create a Run of a built-in Flow, owned by the caller, and start its
workflow. At the Queue limit of the Project it would start in, it is
refused (409 `queueFull`, its message counting both): the caller holds
as many places in their Queue as the limit, a place being a Run waiting
on them at a Gate or a question, or a Run of a Flow with a Gate that has
not reached one yet (`GET /runs/waiting` lists both). The Runs under
way go on.

Find the Runs that opened some pull requests: for each one, the newest
Run the caller can see on their team's board (theirs, or a team
member's on a task they can see), with its Steps, where it is, and the
merge Gate it waits on. A pull request no such Run opened is left out,
whether no Run opened it or one the caller cannot see did.

get.summary:
List the caller's Runs that wait on them at a Gate no one answered
yet, a Flow's Gate no Standing Rule answered or an agent's question,
newest first, each with the Steps it took; and, apart, those that hold
a place in their Queue before asking anything (`starting`).
Read one of the caller's Runs and the Steps it took.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

post.summary:
Cancel one of the caller's Runs. Its running Step or Gate stops, and
reading the Run shows it `cancelled` once its workflow recorded that.
Cancelling a cancelled Run again is accepted and changes nothing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

post.summary:
Answer, as the caller, the Gate one of their Runs waits on. The Run
goes on once its workflow took the answer; reading the Run shows the
answer once it is recorded. A Gate asks a person: the owner's own
signed-in session answers it, and an agent session they work with
(such as the Orchestrator in Macro chat), from its code, answers only
what a Standing Rule could: never an agent's question, a Gate its Flow
keeps for a person, approving a merge or a Tampered Run, nor an
approving answer the Run's Orchestrator Definition does not allow
(403 `reservedForAPerson`); only from a chat, never from a routine's
run or a factory Step's own session. A Gate answered since is a
conflict (409). Any other caller is refused (403).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

post.summary:
Send the agent of the running Step `seq` of one of the caller's Runs a
note, from its Step Terminal. The agent reads it once its turn ends, or
at once when it works on none, and the Step waits for it to answer: it
ends with the agent's latest hand back. Only the Run's owner, in their
own signed-in session, steers a Step (403 otherwise). A Step that ended
(409), or takes no steering now: paused, asked to stop, between its
agent's turns, or with no agent session (409). A blank note, or one
past 4096 bytes, is refused (400); a session that did not take it is
502.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

post.summary:
Pause the running Step `seq` of one of the caller's Runs: its agent's
turn stops, and the Step holds until it is resumed or stopped. The time
it is paused does not count against the Step's wait for its agent, but
a Step still paused when its two hours run out ends `failed`. As for a
note: only the owner in person (403), a Step that ended or takes no
steering now, such as one already paused (409).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

post.summary:
Reply, as the caller, in words to the Gate one of their Runs waits on.
The factory reads the words as one of the Gate's answers, kept as its
note, or asks back on the Gate, which then still waits; an agent's
question takes them as the answer. Reading the Run shows which. Only
the owner's own signed-in session replies (403 otherwise).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

post.summary:
Resume the paused Step `seq` of one of the caller's Runs: its agent is
told to go on where it left off, with the owner's note if they wrote
one, and the Step follows that turn. As for a note: only the owner in
person (403), a Step that ended or is not paused (409), a note past 4096
bytes (400), a session that did not take it (502), which leaves the
Step paused.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

post.summary:
Stop the running Step `seq` of one of the caller's Runs: its agent's
turn stops, and the Step ends `failed`, its session stopped for good;
the Flow routes the failure. As for a note: only the owner in person
(403), a Step that ended or takes no steering now (409).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The place, among the Run's Steps, of the Step whose Gate it answers.

put.summary:
Link one of the caller's Runs to a Macro task they can see,
replacing any task it had.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The Run's id.

get.summary:
The Step of one of the caller's Runs that works, or worked, in an agent
session: the session's view tells the person to steer it from its Run.
A session no Step of theirs works in is not found (404).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: The agent session's id.

get.summary:
The Control File patterns the caller's Runs are checked against: their
team's, or the factory's default, and whether the caller may change
them.

put.summary:
Set the Control File patterns the Runs of the caller's team are checked
against, or go back to the factory's default. Only an admin or the owner
of the team sets them, and a shorter list lets a Run's agent change more
files unseen, so only in their own signed-in session (403 otherwise).

get.summary:
The Standing Rules the caller's Runs are created with: their team's, or
the factory's default, the team's Projects' own, and whether the caller
may change them.

put.summary:
Set the Orchestrator Definition of the caller's team, or go back to the
factory's default. It applies to Runs created from now on. Only an admin
or the owner of the team sets it, in their own signed-in session (403
otherwise): a rule answers Gates in its place.

Set the Orchestrator Definition of the caller's team for one Project,
which replaces the team's for Runs created on a task in it, or remove
it. The caller must administer the team, in their own signed-in session
(403 otherwise), and be able to edit the Project (400 otherwise, as for
one that does not exist).

parameters.name: project_id
parameters.description: The Project: an initiative's id.

get.summary:
List the caller's Runs on a task they can see, newest first, each with
the Steps it took. Other people's Runs on the task are not listed.

parameters.name: task_id
parameters.description: The task document's id.

AgentName.description:
The name the factory's agent definition gives an Agent: a harness, a
model and its instructions.

AnswerGateRequest.description: Request body for answering a Gate.

answer.description: The answer, one the Gate offers.

approvedControlFiles.description:
The Control Files the Run's branch changed unasked that the person
saw and approves: required to approve a Gate of a Tampered Run, and
must be exactly its `controlFiles.tampered` (empty when `unlisted`).

note.description: What the person adds, for the Run's later Steps to read.

AskedBack.description:
A reply the factory could not read as one of a Gate's answers, so it
asked the person back.

Automation.description:
A team's standing order to start a Run of a Flow when its trigger fires.
Its Runs are its creator's, as if they had started them.

createdBy.description: Who created it: the owner of the Runs it starts.

flow.description: The built-in Flow its Runs walk, by name.

repoUrl.description: The repository its Runs work on, for a Flow that works on one.

requestTemplate.description: What its Runs are asked to do.

routineId.description:
The Macro routine that fires it, for a schedule, a repository event
or a Task event, once it is made.

AutomationRequest.description: A new Automation, as a person asks for it.

flow.description: The built-in Flow its Runs walk, one `GET /flows` lists.

name.description: What the team calls it, 1 to 120 characters.

repoUrl.description:
The GitHub repository its Runs work on, as its
`https://github.com/owner/name` URL: required by a Flow that works
on one, and by a repository event, whose repository it is.

requestTemplate.description: What its Runs are asked to do.

oneOf.description: A schedule, as a Macro routine's cron trigger.

cron.description:
Six fields: seconds, minutes, hours, day of month, month and
weekday, such as `0 0 9 * * Mon-Fri`.

timezone.description:
The IANA time zone the schedule is read in, such as
`Europe/Lisbon`.

oneOf.description:
A delivery from Macro's GitHub App about the Automation's
repository.

actions.description: Payload actions, such as `opened`; any when empty.

events.description:
GitHub event names, such as `push` or `pull_request`: at least
one.

oneOf.description: A call to the Automation's webhook, signed with its secret.

A task's property gaining one of some values, such as its status
becoming `In Progress` or its tags gaining one.

propertyId.description: The property definition that must change, such as the status's.

values.description:
Select option ids or referenced entity ids, one of which the
change must add; any change to the property when empty.

AutomationTrigger.description: What starts an Automation's Runs, with the kind's own settings.

AutomationsSettings.description: A team's Automations, for one of its members.

automations.description:
The team's Automations, newest first, at most
[`TEAM_AUTOMATIONS_LISTED`].

isAdmin.description:
Whether the person may change any of them, as a team admin; anyone
may change their own.

teamId.description: The team; none when the person is on no team, and so has none.

BoardNext.description:
Where the board's next page starts: past this Run, in the board's order
(newest first).

createdAt.description: When the last Run the page listed was created.

oneOf.description:
Where the next page starts, past the last Run listed; none on the
last.

runs.description:
The Runs, newest first: never a team member's Run on a task the
caller cannot see.

stoppedEarly.description:
Whether the board stopped reading past Runs the caller cannot see
before the Runs ran out (some 250 of them in a row): older Runs they
see may be there, which no next page reaches. Only on a board no
filter or search narrows.

BoardRun.description: One Run on the board, with where it is.

taskName.description: The name of the task it works on; none without a task.

BoardState.description: Where a Run is, as the board groups it.

CheckResult.description: How one check of a verified round ran.

exitCode.description: Its exit code: 0 when it passed.

output.description: The end of what it printed, both streams, at most 4 KiB.

CheckRound.description:
One round of the repository's checks a Step ran on its agent's work, in
the agent's session.

checkedCommit.description:
The commit a verified round's checks run on: the head of the Run's
branch on GitHub when its first check ran.

checks.description: The names of the checks it runs, in the repository's order.

oneOf.description: How and when it ended; none while the checks run.

results.description:
How each check of a verified round ran so far, in the round's
order; none for a round the agent reports.

verified.description:
Whether the engine runs the checks itself, on the pushed commit in a
worktree of its own, reading each one's exit code; otherwise the
agent runs them and reports how they went.

CheckRoundEnd.description: A round of checks that has ended.

report.description:
What each check did, for a person and for the agent's fix to read:
the agent's report, or, for a verified round, the checks that failed
with the end of their output.

CheckRoundOutcome.description: How a round of a Step's checks ended.

ControlFileChanges.description:
The Control Files a Run's branch changed: files that decide whether the
repository's checks pass, such as its tests, lint configuration and CI
workflows. The Run is Tampered when it changed one its request does not
ask for, and merges only once a person approves them.

named.description:
The files its request asks for by naming them, which need no
approval: empty when `unlisted`.

tampered.description:
The files its request does not ask for, from the repository's root,
in GitHub's order: empty when `unlisted`.

unlisted.description:
GitHub could not list all of the branch's changes, or they were more
than a Run keeps (300 a list), so which Control Files it changed is
not known.

ControlFilesSettings.description:
The Control File patterns a person's Runs are checked against: their
team's, or the factory's default.

canEdit.description: Whether the person may change them: they administer the team.

isDefault.description:
Whether they are the factory's default: the team set none, or the
person is on no team.

patterns.description:
The glob patterns, matched against each changed path from the
repository's root, ignoring case.

teamId.description:
The team whose patterns they are; none when the person is on no
team.

CreateRunRequest.description: Request body for creating a Run.

flow.description: The name of the built-in Flow the Run walks, one `GET /flows` lists.

repoUrl.description:
The GitHub repository the Run works on, as its
`https://github.com/owner/name` URL: required by a Flow that works
on one, such as `code`, and refused by the others. The caller's
linked GitHub account must reach it.

request.description: What the Run is asked to do.

taskId.description: The Macro task the Run works on: its task document's id.

CreatedAutomation.description:
A new Automation, and the secret its webhook's calls are signed with:
shown once, when it is made.

webhookSecret.description:
For a webhook, the secret its calls are signed with: the factory
never shows it again.

DurationStats.description: A spread of durations: how many, their median and 90th percentile.

EntryId.description: The id of one of a Flow's entries. A Step is a visit of an entry.

EntryInsight.description: One of a Flow's entries, across the period's Runs.

oneOf.description: How long its Steps took, a cancelled Run's left out.

entry.description: The entry's id, as its Flow names it.

failedRuns.description: The Runs in which one of its Steps failed.

oneOf.description: Its Gate, if its Steps opened one.

outcomes.description: How its Steps ended, most often first.

revisitedRuns.description:
The Runs that visited it more than once: sent back to it, or started
over.

oneOf.description: The tokens its agent Steps used, if any recorded usage.

trouble.description: The newest Runs where it failed or was visited more than once.

troubledRuns.description:
The Runs in which one of its Steps failed or that visited it more
than once, each counted once.

ErrorResponse.description:
A plain old json error response for use with axum.
yup, thats it.

FindingKind.description: What a finding turned out to be once its round ended.

repeated.description:
Whether an earlier firing with the same key came to this, so this
one started nothing.

oneOf.description: The Run it started.
Why it started none.

FiringSkip.description: Why a firing started no Run.

flow.description: The Flow's name; none for Runs recorded before the Flow was kept.

FlowSummary.description: A Flow a person can start a Run of.

description.description: What it does, for a person.

name.description: Its name, which a Run of it is started with.

repository.description:
Whether a Run of it works on a GitHub repository, which starting it
must name.

FlowsResponse.description: The Flows a Run can be started of.

Gate.description: A question a Step's end puts to a person. The Run waits for the answer.

oneOf.description: The person's answer; none while the Run waits.

answers.description: The answers it offers, in the Flow's order.

oneOf.description:
The latest reply the factory could not read as one of its answers,
and asked back for; none when it never asked back.

kind.description: Who asks it: the Flow, or the Step's agent.

oneOf.description:
The stand-in's answer for the Run's owner, while the owner may
override it and after; none when the stand-in did not answer.

GateAnswer.description:
The answer to a Gate: a person's, a Standing Rule's (a Rule Answer), or
the stand-in's for the Run's owner.

agentSessionId.description:
The agent session that gave the answer for the owner, when the
Orchestrator did rather than the owner in person; it is then not
counted among the owner's own answers.

answer.description: The answer, one the Gate offered: the outcome the Flow routes.

approvedControlFiles.description:
The Run's Tampered files the person approved with their answer: an
empty list approves a Run whose changes GitHub could not list. None
when the answer approved none.

byStandIn.description:
Whether the answer is the stand-in's, which the owner let stand
([`Gate::stand_in`] says why it gave it).

note.description: What the person added, for the Run's later Steps to read.

replyConfidence.description:
For a person's answer the factory read from their words (kept as its
note), how sure it was, in percent; none for an answer given with a
button, and for any answer not a person's.

oneOf.description:
The Standing Rule that answered, for a Rule Answer; none for a
person's.

Who answered; none once their account is gone, and for a Rule
Answer.

GateInsight.description: A Gate's questions and their answers.

answers.description: How often each answer was given, most given first.

oneOf.description: How long people took to answer.

GateKind.description: Who asks a Gate's question, which says how it is answered.

GithubFiring.description: The GitHub delivery that fired a repository event's Automation.

branch.description:
The branch it is about: a push's, a pull request's head, or a
workflow run's or check suite's head branch.

HandBackRequest.description: Request body for handing back an agent Step's result.

outcome.description: How the Step ended: one of the outcomes it offers.

text.description: What the agent produced, for the Run's later Steps and for people.

InsightDay.description: The Runs created on one day of the period.

date.description: The day, in the period's time zone.

Lines.description: The lines of a file a finding is about, from 1, both included.

end.description: The last line; the first, for one line.

LinkTaskRequest.description: Request body for linking a Run to a task.

MainHold.description:
A hold on a base branch whose required checks failed. It lasts until the
checks on the base's head pass again.

failed.description: The checks that failed, one line each, with their pages.

headSha.description: The base's head commit, as the checks were last seen failing on it.

since.description: When the base was first seen red, in this red period.

taskId.description:
The task filed with the merges made since the base was last green:
its task document's id, once it is filed. None before then, or once
the task document is deleted.

NamedCount.description: A name a Flow gives (an outcome, a Gate's answer) and how often it came.

name.description: The name, as the Flow writes it.

NoteStepRequest.description: Request body for a note to a running Step's agent.

note.description:
The owner's words, for the agent to take into account: at most 4096
bytes, not blank.

OrchestratorDefinition.description:
A workspace's Orchestrator Definition: which kinds of Gate the factory
decides on its own, whether the Gates it leaves go to the Run's owner,
which the stand-in answers for the Run's owner when no rule does, and
the Queue limit at which no new Run starts. A kind left off waits for
a person, as every Gate did before Standing
Rules. Whatever it says, a Tampered Run's Gates and a merge through a
Main Hold stay a person's.

blockers.description:
Send a review round's Blockers to be fixed (`fix_blockers`), for at
most two fix rounds in a row; Blockers found after those go to a
person.

merge.description:
Merge once CI is green, nothing is Tampered and the base branch has
no Main Hold (`merge_when_green`).

orchestrator.description:
The kinds of Gate the Orchestrator, the owner's agent in Macro chat,
may give the approving answer to for them (`approve`, `fix`); off
for every kind when left out. It may always send work back, and
never approves a merge.

ownerGates.description:
The owner section: a Gate no rule answers goes to the Run's owner.
They are notified, and the Gate is listed as waiting on them; a
review round whose Blockers are the round before's, unchanged after
a rule sent those to a fix, waits for them rather than another fix;
and what they comment on the Run's task once a Gate opened reaches
the next agent Step. Off, the factory leaves those Gates waiting as
before. A definition sent without it has it off.

queueLimit.description:
The Queue limit: the most places a person may hold in their Queue
under this definition. A place is a Run of theirs waiting on them at
a Gate or a question, or a Run of a Flow with a Gate that has not
reached one yet. A new Run of theirs starts only while they hold
fewer places than the limit; Runs already going go on. None, and a
definition sent without it, sets no limit. From [`MIN_QUEUE_LIMIT`]
to [`MAX_QUEUE_LIMIT`]. A Run does not keep it: it decides only
whether a Run starts, so a Run's rules read with none.

standIn.description:
The kinds of Gate the stand-in answers for the Run's owner, after
the rules and before the person; off for every kind when left out.

taskThread.description:
The task thread section: a Run on a task posts its main updates
(its start, each Step's end, its Gates, its pull request, its merge
and how it ended) to one comment thread on the task, as its owner.
Off, as when a definition is sent without it, a Run posts nothing.

OrchestratorKinds.description:
The kinds of Gate the Orchestrator may give the approving answer to for
the Run's owner. It never approves a merge, so it has no setting for
one.

blockers.description: Send a review round's Blockers to be fixed.

Outcome.description:
How a Step ended, in the words of its Flow (`done`, `clean`, `blockers`,
...). The Flow decides where each outcome takes the Run.

OutcomeCounts.description: How many Runs went each way: still going, or ended with each outcome.

blocked.description: Runs that ran out of visits, or of Steps, with nowhere to go.

manual.description: Runs that ended for a person to take over.

success.description: Runs whose Flow reached its successful end.

PassedOver.description:
An Agent that could not start a Step, so the next Agent of its Role took
it.

reason.description: Why it could not start, as a code such as `ai_allowance_exhausted`.

ProjectRules.description: A Project's own Standing Rules, which its team set.

definition.description: Which kinds of Gate its rules decide.

PullRequestRun.description: The Run that opened a pull request, as the board shows it.

listed.description: The Run, where it is, and its task's name.

mergeGateSeq.description:
The Step whose merge Gate the Run waits on, by its place among the
Run's Steps: approving it is how the pull request merges. None while
the Run is anywhere else.

url.description: The pull request's page, as the lookup named it.

PullRequestRuns.description: The Runs that opened some pull requests.

runs.description:
One for each pull request a Run the caller can see opened, its
newest such Run, in the lookup's order; none for a pull request no
such Run opened.

PullRequestUrls.description: GitHub pull requests, by their pages.

urls.description:
The pull requests' pages, such as
`https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/12`: at most 100.

ReplyToGateRequest.description: Request body for replying to a Gate in words.

reply.description: The person's words, in place of one of the Gate's answers.

Repository.description: The GitHub repository a Run works on.

baseBranch.description:
The branch the Run's work starts from and proposes its change to: the
repository's default when the Run started.

RequiredChecksState.description: Why a base branch's required checks decide nothing.

ResumeStepRequest.description: Request body for resuming a paused Step.

note.description:
The owner's words for the agent as it goes on, if any: at most 4096
bytes; a blank note is left out.

ReviewFinding.description: A finding as its round keeps it.

blocksAnywhere.description:
Whether it blocks wherever it is: a Blocker of the round before
found again, or a reviewer's answer that never read.

followUpTaskId.description:
The follow-up task it became, when it is a follow-up and the task
was made: its task document's id.

oneOf.description: What it turned out to be; none while its round reviews.
The lines it is about; none for the whole file.

path.description: The file, from the repository's root.

place.description: Its place among what the reviewer handed back, from 1.

oneOf.description: The Role of the reviewer that found it.

seq.description: The reviewer's Step: its place among the Run's Steps.

ReviewRound.description: One round of a Run's review panel.

diffBase.description:
Where the diff under review starts: the Run's base branch, or the
commit the round before reviewed; none for a round that could not
open.

oneOf.description: How and when it ended; none while it reviews.

failure.description:
Why it could not open, as when the Run's branch is gone: it then
ran no reviewer and ended failed.

findings.description: What its reviewers found, by Step and place.

fixDiff.description:
Whether it reviews the fix diff, the changes made since the round
before, rather than the Run's whole change.

headSha.description:
The commit of the Run's branch it reviews; none for a round that
could not open.

reviewers.description: How many reviewers it has, each in a Step of its own.

round.description:
Which round of the Run it is, from 1, counting every round the Run
recorded: a reset of its entry does not count again from 1.

seq.description:
The place of its first Step among the Run's Steps; its reviewers'
Steps take this place and the ones after it.

visit.description:
Which round of its entry it is since the entry was last reset, from
1, as the entry's round limit counts them: a round after a reset
(as when a person sends the change back) is visit 1 again, and
reviews the whole change.

ReviewRoundEnd.description: A review round that has ended.

Role.description:
A job in a Flow, such as `planner`, `writer`, `reviewer` or `fixer`. An
entry whose Step an agent does names the Role, and the factory's agent
definition lists the Agents that may fill it.

RoutineFiring.description: What fired an Automation, from its routine's run.

firing.description: The routine run's id: a retried run fires once.

oneOf.description: The GitHub delivery a repository event is.

taskId.description: The task a Task event is about.

RulesSource.description: Where a Run's Standing Rules came from.

oneOf.description:
The Automation that started it, as it was then; none for a Run a
person started.

The Control Files its branch changed, as the pull request Steps last
read them. None when it changed none.

createdInPerson.description:
Whether its owner created it in their own signed-in session, from an
account that is not an agent's: only then does its request ask for
the Control Files it names.

oneOf.description: How and when it ended; none while it runs.

flow.description:
The built-in Flow it walks, by name; none only for a Run recorded
before Runs kept it.

id.description: The Run's id, also its Temporal workflow id.

projectId.description:
The Project (an initiative) its task was in when it was created,
kept as a record: none without a task or Project, and for a Run
created before Runs kept it.

pullRequestUrl.description:
The page of the pull request its branch proposes its change in, as
the pull request Steps last found it; none until one is found.

oneOf.description:
The GitHub repository the Run works on; none for a Run that works on
no code.

request.description: What the Run was asked to do.

oneOf.description:
The Standing Rules that answer its Gates, as they were when it was
created; none for a Run created before Runs kept them, whose Gates
all wait for a person.

taskId.description:
The Macro task the Run works on: its task document's id. None when
the Run has no task, or its task was deleted.

userId.description: Who started the Run: its agent Steps run as them.

RunAutomation.description: The Automation that started a Run, as it was then.

id.description: The Automation's id; it may have been deleted since.

name.description: Its name when it started the Run.

trigger.description: What kind of trigger started the Run.

RunDetail.description: A Run and the Steps it took.

oneOf.description:
Why the checks the base branch requires decide nothing, while the
Run is at its merge: they could not be read, or the base requires
none. Nothing holds the merge on them.

The Main Hold on the base branch the Run merges to, while the Run
is at its merge and the base's required checks fail: the Run does
not merge until it clears, even once its merge Gate is approved.

reviewRounds.description: Its review rounds, in order, each with what its reviewers found.

steps.description: Its Steps, in the order they started.

RunEnd.description: A Run that has ended: how, and when.

RunErrorCode.description: Why a request was refused, where a client acts on the cause.

RunErrorResponse.description:
What a refused or failed request answers: a message, and for a refusal
a client acts on, its code.

oneOf.description: Why it was refused, when a client acts on the cause.

RunInsights.description: How a person's Runs went over a period.

capped.description:
Whether the period had more Runs than that, so the oldest are left
out.

days.description: The Runs created each day of the period, every day listed.

entries.description: The Flows' entries the Runs visited, in their Flows' order.

flow.description: The Flow read, or none for every Flow.

flows.description: The Runs of each Flow, most Runs first.

runCap.description: The most Runs read: the newest in the period.

oneOf.description:
How long Runs took from creation to their end, cancelled Runs and
Runs still going left out.

timeZone.description: The time zone its days are in.

RunLink.description: One of the period's Runs, to link to.

oneOf.description: How it ended; none while it goes.

title.description: The first line of its request.

RunRules.description: The Standing Rules a Run keeps from when it was created.

definition.description: Which kinds of Gate its rules decide.

projectId.description:
The Project (an initiative) they were set for, when they are a
Project's.

RunTokens.description: One of the period's Runs and the tokens its agent Steps used.

SessionStepRef.description: The factory Step an agent session works in, as its owner reads it.

runId.description: The Run the Step belongs to.

seq.description: The Step's place among the Run's Steps.

SetAutomationEnabledRequest.description: Request body for switching an Automation on or off.

SetControlFilesRequest.description: Request body for setting the Control File patterns.

patterns.description:
The glob patterns, matched against each changed path from the
repository's root: `*` stays within one folder, `**` spans any
number. At most 200, each at most 256 bytes. Null goes back to the
factory's default; an empty list checks no file.

SetStandingRulesRequest.description: Request body for setting an Orchestrator Definition.

oneOf.description:
Which kinds of Gate the factory answers on its own. Null goes back
to the factory's default (a team's), or removes the Project's own
(a Project's).

StandInAnswer.description:
The stand-in's answer to a Gate, for the Run's owner: the answer it
gives, why, and until when the owner may override it.

answer.description: Its answer, one the Gate offers.

confidence.description: How sure it was, in percent.

reason.description: Why, in a sentence or two.

until.description: Until when the owner may override it; then the Run goes on with it.

StandInKinds.description:
The kinds of Gate the stand-in answers for the Run's owner: a small
model that answers as the owner would, which the owner may override for
a short while. It never answers a merge Gate, so it has no setting for
one.

blockers.description: Answer a review round's Blockers Gate.

StandingRule.description:
A Standing Rule: the answer the factory gives a Gate of one kind on its
own, when what the rule requires holds.

StandingRulesSettings.description:
The Standing Rules a person's Runs are created with: their team's
Orchestrator Definition, or the factory's default, and the team's
Projects' own, which replace it for a Run whose task is in one.

canEdit.description: Whether the person may change them: they administer the team.

definition.description: Which kinds of Gate the factory answers on its own.

isDefault.description:
Whether it is the factory's default: the team set none, or the
person is on no team.

projects.description: The team's Projects that have their own, by the initiative's id.

teamId.description: The team whose rules they are; none when the person is on no team.

Steer.description: One thing the Run's owner did to a running Step.

note.description: Their note to the agent, for a note or a resume that has one.

undelivered.description:
Whether the agent's session refused the note or the resume, so the
agent never read it.

SteerAction.description: What the Run's owner did to a running Step from its Step Terminal.

Step.description: One visit of one of a Run's entries.

oneOf.description: The Agent that took the Step, from its Role's Agents.

checks.description:
The rounds of the repository's checks it ran, in order: none for a
Step that runs no checks.

oneOf.description: How and when it ended; none while it runs.
The question its end put to a person, if its entry has a Gate.

passedOver.description:
The Agents before it that could not start the Step, in order, and
why.

oneOf.description: The Role an agent filled for the Step; none for a Step no agent does.

seq.description: The Step's place among the Run's Steps, from 1.

terminal.description:
Its Step Terminal: the session its owner may watch, and how they
steered it.

visit.description: Which visit of the entry it is, from 1.

StepEnd.description: A Step that has ended: its outcome, what it produced, and when.

output.description: What the Step produced, for a person to read.

StepTerminal.description:
A running agent Step as its owner watches and steers it, from the Run
view: the agent session to watch, whether it is paused or asked to stop,
and what the owner did, oldest first.

betweenTurns.description:
Whether its agent works on no turn the Step waits on now, as while
the factory runs the repository's checks itself: the Step takes no
steering until the factory's next prompt.

endsBy.description:
When a paused Step ends, failed, unless it is resumed first: its
work's time runs out then. Set by the Run API while it is paused.

pauseRanOutAt.description: When its work ended it because it stayed paused past its time.

pausedAt.description: Since when the owner paused the Step, while it is paused.

sessionId.description:
The agent session the Step works in, while it runs in one: none for a
Step that ended, let go of its session, or does no agent work.

steers.description: What the owner did, oldest first.

stopAskedAt.description:
When the owner asked the Step to stop; it ends `failed` once its
agent's turn stops.

TaskRunsResponse.description: A task's Runs, as the caller sees them.

runs.description: The caller's Runs on the task, newest first: at most the newest 50.

cacheRead.description: Input tokens read from the prompt cache.

cacheWrite.description: Input tokens written to the prompt cache.

input.description: Input tokens, besides those read from or written to the prompt cache.

TriggerKind.description: What starts an Automation's Runs, as a kind.

TroubleRun.description: A Run where an entry failed or was visited more than once.

failed.description: Whether one of the entry's Steps in it failed.

visits.description: How many times it visited the entry.

UsageInsight.description: What the period's agent Steps used.

agentSteps.description: Steps an agent worked on, in a session.

heaviest.description: The Runs that used the most tokens, most first.

measuredSteps.description:
Those whose session has usage recorded. An agent that runs on a
person's own computer records none.

WaitingRunsResponse.description: The caller's Runs that hold a place in their Queue.

runs.description:
The caller's Runs that have not ended and wait on a Gate no one
answered yet, newest first: at most the newest 50.

starting.description:
The caller's Runs of a Flow with a Gate that have not ended or
reached a Gate yet, newest first, at most the newest 50: each holds
the place it will ask for. Cancelling one frees it.

WebhookFiring.description:
What a webhook call may carry, as its JSON body; an empty body carries
nothing.

taskId.description: The task the Run works on, which the Automation's creator must see.

tags.name: factory
tags.description: Runs of the software factory's Flows
